title: Deeper/broader cross-project interoperability and failure-localization refresh
scope: Recheck normative Autodesk DXF group-code ordering and SPLINE field contracts
Cross-map current ACadSharp DWG/DXF reports for whole-file rejection, SPLINE output, MLeader context objects, and recursive DXF parsing
Reconcile LibreDWG conversion-integrity reports with existing output closure and record-identity gates
Reconcile FreeCAD's documented converter-to-DXF-to-importer route with converter-success verification
Refine implementation readiness without adding peer execution or per-slice test cost

method.kind: Read-only review of primary Autodesk documentation, public project documentation/issues, and local plan/source/test inventory
method.limitations: Issue reports remain reporter evidence, not normative rules or local reproductions. ACadSharp #1299's linked drawing archive was not downloaded; its report supplies no raw SPLINE arrays or exact GDAL diagnostics. Mutable master documentation was inspected as of 2026-10-17 and is not an immutable release qualification.

sources.observed: The object/entity processing guidance says entity group-code order may vary and recommends table-driven processing and ignoring undefined codes. This does not authorize reordering compound or repeated sequences.

The DXF table distinguishes degree and count fields, repeated knot/weight values, control points, fit points, and optional start/end tangents. It is a wire-field reference, not a complete curve-validity oracle.

sources.revision: open issue body reviewed 2026-10-17; report names AutoCAD 2025 and ACadSharp 3.8.14/master or 3.8.0
sources.observed: The report says AutoCAD 2025 rejects a whole AC1032 file containing an MTEXT with frame-only background flags, while a combined flag and an AC1027 file reportedly open. The reporter says one MTEXT object's bytes matched an AutoCAD object after a writer change, but could not isolate the whole-file cause; missing VisualStyle/detail-view objects are a hypothesis only.

sources.revision: open issue body and maintainer response reviewed 2026-10-17; report names AutoCAD LT 2026 and ACadSharp 3.7.16
sources.observed: The reporter says a no-op AC1032 DWG rewrite failed native AUDIT and removed standalone AcDbMLeaderObjectContextData objects. The report distinguishes DWG extension-dictionary-owned context objects from DXF MLEADER entity fields. No shareable DWG is attached.

sources.revision: open issue body reviewed 2026-10-17; reporter names NuGet v3.8.0
sources.observed: The reporter says DWG-to-DXF output contains SPLINE data rejected by GDAL. The issue provides no offending handle, raw SPLINE arrays, expected curve, or exact GDAL error details; a linked archive was not downloaded.

sources.revision: open issue body reviewed 2026-10-17; report names ACadSharp 3.8.0/master
sources.observed: The report describes recursive parsing of long comment, XDATA application-block, and WIPEOUT clip-boundary runs, with generated 20,000-item sequences causing process stack exhaustion in the cited reader. The threshold is peer/platform-specific.
The report describes a DWG-to-DXF path that can stop before ENTITIES/EOF while returning exit status zero; this is a peer output-integrity report, not a local result.
The report describes an INSERT with group 66=1 but no ATTRIB/SEQEND chain in one generated conversion route; it does not prove a matching libdxfrw failure.
FreeCAD describes DWG import as an external converter producing DXF followed by the selected DXF importer; this is a composed route, not native FreeCAD DWG decoding.

The report concerns the reverse DXF-to-DWG export wrapper: automatic mode may return after a failed converter without verifying output or reaching later alternatives. It is a FreeCAD wrapper report, not evidence about the DWG-import wrapper, libdxfrw behavior, or all packaged FreeCAD releases.

sources.revision: working-tree plan over baseline de27a3391a624aba03ca71f3583c4b3a6e6396a9 reviewed 2026-10-17
sources.observed: The reports map to existing SPLINE, DWG object graph, bounded DXF parser, output closure, and FreeCAD composed-consumer owners. Existing tests already cover the narrow MTEXT 0/16/17 body vector and repeated-record safety classes; no duplicate owner is justified.

assessment.wireRule: Follow Autodesk's order-flexibility guidance only for independent fields. Repeated arrays, subclass scopes, XDATA, child-record sequences, and opaque payload chunks retain their format-defined order.
assessment.dwgWriterAcceptance: Exact entity-body bytes and successful self-read do not establish full-document acceptance. Compare object/type/handle/owner closure, required sections, diagnostics, and native audit separately.
assessment.splineEvidence: A downstream parser error is an interoperability signal, not a semantic oracle. Any local investigation needs raw per-handle arrays, exact version/route, parser diagnostic, and independently expected curve geometry.
assessment.converterEvidence: For DWG import, pin the converter and importer separately; verify fresh DXF output, process status, target version, strict parsing, and source-to-output manifest before scoring the importer result. Treat reverse DXF-to-DWG fallback behavior as a separate consumer route.
assessment.implementationSpeed: Reuse existing source-generated selectors and owning CTests; keep peer/native/fuzz/full-suite work at the existing composed or scheduled checkpoint.
